verdict.rationale: mise automations are tasks defined in mise.toml or as standalone script files, and the config is meant to be checked into git. That lets users version and review them through ordinary source control, and pinning plus committed lockfiles make tool versions reproducible. Versioning, review and rollback all depend on external git, and mise ships no native history or undo of its own; the closest built-in review aid is `mise lock --bump --dry-run`, which previews tool version bumps rather than task changes. Missing for 10: native automation version history, a built-in review/diff workflow for task changes, documented rollback of automations, and independent corroboration of this workflow.
